parameter.illustration: Illustration changes with the setting; it is not a measurement of your recording.
parameter.highpass: Removes low rumble below this frequency. Raising it cleans more bass but can thin the voice.
parameter.lowMid: Changes the body of the voice around 250 Hz. Lower it to reduce muddiness; raise it for warmth.
parameter.presence: Changes clarity around 3.2 kHz. Raising it helps consonants stand out; too much can sound sharp.
parameter.lowpass: Reduces frequencies above this cutoff. Lowering it softens hiss and high detail.
parameter.threshold: Compression starts around this RMS level. Lowering the threshold compresses more of the voice; it is not a peak ceiling.
parameter.ratio: Controls how strongly loud passages are reduced. Higher ratios make levels more even but reduce natural dynamics.
parameter.attack: How quickly compression reacts to a loud onset. Short attack softens peaks; long attack preserves their punch.
parameter.release: How quickly compression relaxes after a loud passage. Short release recovers faster; long release sounds smoother.
parameter.makeup: Raises the level after compression. With loudness normalization enabled, the final average level still follows the loudness target.
parameter.gateThreshold: Quiet passages below this RMS level are reduced. Raising it catches more breaths and noise, but may affect quiet word endings.
parameter.gateReduction: How much quiet passages are reduced. Zero disables attenuation; larger values suppress more background without deleting time.
parameter.targetLufs: Sets average perceived loudness for playback and export. A higher target sounds louder; the peak ceiling may limit the gain.
parameter.truePeak: Limits the measured true peak during normalization, including peaks between samples. A lower ceiling leaves more headroom by reducing overall gain.
parameter.volume: Changes track level after effects and normalization. Positive gain can raise peaks above the normalization ceiling.
parameter.pan: Moves the sound between left and right speakers. The centre preserves both channels; moving right reduces the left channel.
effects.loudnessHint: Measured before playback and export. Changes are remeasured on the next start. Peak headroom can keep the result below the target; live microphone monitoring is not normalized.
